Professor Erdal is one of the best instructors I have encountered in my academic journey so far. He is very compassionate toward students and explains concepts using different real-life examples, from simple daily situations to more advanced cases. This approach makes the course much easier to understand. He was highly successful in teaching all the concepts with great clarity and quality.

Erdal Hoca is always interested in whether the class actually understood the topic, and continues explaining until everybody understands. He does not just do everything once and move on. However, for 95% of the time, he uses Excel for the classes, but expects the students to solve the questions by hand in the exams. He does not solve any questions by hand, therefore it is hard for the students to understand how to proceed in the exam. He even organized an extra session before the exam to solve similar problems in order to prepare the students, yet he still used Excel even when the students explicitly asked him to solve by hand.

The instructor is a kind and genuinely pleasant person, and it is clear that they care about students. However, due to their age and pace, the lectures were often quite slow and the class was not very active. course: A clear positive of the course is that the topic itself is genuinely interesting and valuable. However, the main downside is that the material remained quite basic and did not translate well into practical understanding. We covered the concepts at a surface level, but there were limited real-world examples, applications, or hands-on practice to make the content feel concrete and usable.

This course includes many different concepts, and the instructor needs to teach students with different academic backgrounds. In my opinion, Erdal Hocam was very successful in managing this challenge. As a small suggestion, having at least one session at the end of the semester focused on the investing part (e.g., Markowitz model) would be helpful for MBA students.

Since students are already allowed to bring a cheat sheet to the exam, my suggestion is to apply stricter limitations on it. Formulas are difficult to memorize and easy to confuse, so the cheat sheet is helpful. However, it should be restricted to fewer pages. Some students may misuse this by writing some other information instead of essential formulas or points, which can make the efforts of students who genuinely study and prepare appear average.
